thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: multiple GPU OOMs detected on decode-streaming pool (us-west-2). Error signature: CUDA OOM, repeated coredumps, requests dropped. Auto-escalation threshold hit.

oncall_maria: I’m on it. Seeing alerts spike at 03:12 UTC. Initial symptom: influx of long-running decode requests that never close.

eng-runtime_james: I pulled the logs from one of the pods — decode loop kept appending tokens until OOM. Likely a max_tokens or client-side misconfig.

sre_elaine: Can you paste the lines?

eng-runtime_james: ```
[2026-03-15T03:11:58Z] request_id=abc123 route=/chat/stream model=redwood-xl-decode seq=...
...token_count=98321 streaming_chunk_sent=true
[2026-03-15T03:12:02Z] CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 512MB
```

oncall_maria: nvidia-smi on node gpu-27 shows 100% mem used across decode containers. Repro: kill one pod, restarted it, it quickly OOMs again when traffic hits the same route.

product-ops_tyler: Any idea which customers are hitting this? We’re getting inbound CS messages.

customer-success-sam: Two accounts reported timeouts and partial responses in the last 10 minutes (acme-marketing, shopwave). I’ve DM’d them acknowledging impact.

eng-platform_sophie: Quick mitigation idea: enforce per-request token cap at the edge/router (deny > 4096). We have a per-route limit flag; looks like it was unset on a canary route after last config push.

sre_elaine: Can we patch the config and roll without full restart? Prefer not to bounce everything.

eng-platform_sophie: Yes — patch the ConfigMap and trigger a rolling restart for the decode deployment only, or hot-reload route rules if gateway supports it. I’ll prepare the patch.

eng-runtime_james: Also we should route overflow to a fallback lower-memory model (quantized) instead of letting it hit decode nodes. I can add a temporary routing rule to fallback to redwood-quant-2 if token_count > 4096.

oncall_maria: Steps for immediate action: 1) Patch gateway to enforce max_tokens=4096 on /chat/stream 2) Add routing rule to fallback quantized model 3) Cordon problematic node pool 4) Monitor OOM alerts and token metrics

incident-bot: Action assigned: oncall_maria -> patch gateway config. Priority: P0.

oncall_maria: Patching now. Command: ```kubectl -n infra patch configmap gateway-config -p '{"data":{"max_tokens_default":"4096"}}'```

eng-platform_sophie: Gateway hot-reload accepted the patch. Confirming current default: 4096. Pushing routing override for route /chat/stream -> redwood-quant-2 when requested tokens > 4096.

eng-runtime_james: Routing rule applied. Adding drop-protection: if client requests > 4096, respond with 413 + suggested truncation.

sre_elaine: Cordoning nodes with repeating OOMs: `kubectl cordon gpu-27` and evicting pods to other less-loaded nodes. Doing drain with grace 30s.

sre_elaine: Note — draining caused transient 503s for a couple of in-flight streaming sessions. We should message CS.

customer-success-sam: Noted. Sending a short status update to affected customers: "We are mitigating excessive token generation causing OOMs; temporary limits applied; partial responses possible."", sending now.

eng-runtime_james: Verify logs after patch: pods are no longer hitting CUDA OOM. Token histograms show max at ~3800 now. Good.

incident-bot: Alert suppression: temporarily mute repeated CUDA OOM alert rule for decode pool to reduce noise while monitoring.

oncall_maria: Monitoring metrics: request drops down 95% from peak, OOM alarms silenced. Will keep an eye for 30m.

product-ops_tyler: Can you surface the root cause? Why did default become unset? We need post-incident action items.

eng-platform_sophie: Preliminary cause: a recent config merge removed the default per-route max_tokens for canary routes — a YAML block accidentally deleted. It only affected routes deployed in the canary namespace which had low traffic historically until a customer test spiked use.

eng-runtime_james: Repro steps locally: replicate a client sending a very large max_tokens value and stream=1 => decode process keeps allocating KV cache proportional to token length; in our runtime we don’t enforce a hard cap at decode layer. That allowed a single request to consume whole GPU.

sre_elaine: Postmortem action items (prelim): 1) enforce server-side hard token cap in the runtime (fail fast) 2) add config merge validation to CI to prevent removing default blocks 3) add per-request token rate-limiting at gateway 4) make fallback routing automated when a node pool starts OOMing 5) create a customer-impact export for CS.

oncall_maria: Handoff: I’m going to watch for 30 more minutes; if stable, I’ll hand to day oncall @eng-runtime_james at 04:00 UTC.

eng-runtime_james: I’ll take second-shift. Will prepare a short runbook: commands to patch gateway, routing override, node cordon, and metrics dashboards links.

incident-bot: Handoff scheduled: oncall_maria -> eng-runtime_james at 04:00 UTC.

customer-success-sam: Logged impacted requests and customers; will follow up with personalized notes once we have root cause and ETA for a fix.

product-ops_tyler: Thanks team. Please add any config diffs and commands used to the incident ticket. We’ll prep a status page update after the handoff.

eng-platform_sophie: Pushing a guardian rule to CI now to block PRs that remove `max_tokens_default` key from gateway config. CI job name: `config-guard/gateway-max-tokens`.

sre_elaine: Quick note — we saw a pattern where generated text length correlates with KV memory growth; runtime fix should cap KV growth at N tokens per request.

eng-runtime_james: I’ll put up a small PR to add a hard enforcement layer in the runtime that rejects > 16k tokens at the runtime level (safety net) and we can tune down to 8k after testing.

oncall_maria: Final check: metrics steady for 22 minutes, no new OOMs. I’m handing off to @eng-runtime_james.

oncall_maria: Handoff complete. Summary: applied gateway max_tokens=4096, added routing fallback to quantized model, cordoned noisy node, customers notified, alerts muted for noise. Continued action items assigned.

eng-runtime_james: Taking over. I’ll draft the incident timeline and start the postmortem doc. Will include code/CI blocking and runtime caps as follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for active paging; oncall handoff recorded.
